sources.entry: SYM - GUI Application to symbolicate iOS crash log. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/zqqf16/SYM)

summary.one_liner: SYM is a macOS GUI app that symbolicates Apple crash reports (.crash, .ips and related formats) by matching them to dSYM files and turning hex stack addresses into readable symbols.
summary.what_it_does: SYM opens Apple crash reports in classic .crash, IPS and some related JSON formats, or accepts a pasted log in its editor. It searches the Mac for matching dSYMs, including those inside Xcode Archives, and lets you import dSYMs manually. A single action symbolicates the report, with Find (⌘F) and Undo (⌘Z) in the editor. An optional user-supplied download script can fetch dSYMs from a server. It can also connect to a connected iOS device to pull crash logs and browse an app's sandbox. Settings cover font, highlight color, line numbers, summary bar, download folder and script, and hardware model name updates.
use_cases: symbolicate an iOS app crash log on a Mac
find matching dSYM files for a crash report
import crash logs from a connected iPhone
browse an iOS app's sandbox files
download dSYMs from a server with a script
read and search Apple .ips crash reports
how_to_run: Download the app from the Releases page and install it (macOS 13 or later).
For development: clone the repo and open SYM.xcodeproj in Xcode.
make archive (optionally: make archive script=/path/to/download.sh), then make dmg or make install
notable: Finds dSYMs automatically, including inside Xcode Archives, with manual import as fallback
Optional user-provided download script to fetch dSYMs from a server
Connects to iOS devices to import crash logs and browse app sandboxes
Bundled hardware model name list that can be updated in Settings
Makefile covers archive, notarize, DMG and install steps
caveats: Notarization needs a notarytool keychain profile named "Notarization" set up by the user.
Developer build of device libraries requires rebuilding via build.sh in the Device folder.
